text: The 2021 tree-cover loss in the pine plantation was most likely caused by timber harvest. The loss area of 81.3 hectares, observed by the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset, aligns with the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 data, which mapped 98% of the event area as forest in 2020. The Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) forest map confirms that the area is planted forest, specifically with Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda species, with no native forest present. The loss did not occur in patches under 0.5 hectares, ruling out small, scattered events. Therefore, the evidence strongly suggests that the tree-cover loss was due to timber harvest.
